rules.statement: Section 26 of the Partition Law, No. 21 of 1977 delineates the types of orders a court may include in an interlocutory decree in partition actions.
rules.supporting_quote: (1) Section 26 of the Partition Law, No. 21 of 1977 sets out the orders a Court may include in the Interlocutory Decree in an action instituted under section 2 by any co-owner to partition a land owned in common. (2) Although section 18 (a) (viii) makes it obligatory to the Commissioner to include in his report, inter alia, the existing means of access to the land from the nearest public road, neither section 26 nor section 2 gives any right to a District Court to make an order with regard to such a roadway if it fell outside corpus. Section 18 (a) (viii) does not empower the District Court to adjudicate upon such road, if it fell outside the corpus. Per Dissanayake, J. "In my view section 18 (a) (viii) has been included in the Partition Law, No. 21 of 1977 to facilitate the District Court to allot shares to the parties 2 according to the respective rights in an equitable manner, taking into consideration the necessity to grant a right of access to each lot from the nearest public road."

rules.statement: The Commissioner is required to include in his report the existing means of access to the land from the nearest public road, and neither Section 26 nor Section 2 of the relevant act confer a District Court with jurisdiction to make an order regarding such a roadway if it falls outside the corpus.

rules.statement: Section 18(a) does not confer authority on the District Court to determine claims over roads outside its jurisdiction.
